description: Partie 3 — examen blanc n°1 : 13 conversations (dont 2 à trois locuteurs, 3 avec graphique, 2 questions de sens implicite).

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Hi, Daniel. Did the printer paper we ordered last week ever arrive? We're almost out.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Not yet. I called the supplier this morning, and they said there was a problem at their warehouse. It should be here by Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Thursday? We're printing the training manuals for the new hires on Wednesday.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Hmm. There's a stationery store across the street. I could pick up a few packs to get us through until the order arrives.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: That would be great. Just keep the receipt so accounting can reimburse you.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Good evening, and welcome to the Harbor View Hotel. Do you have a reservation?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Yes, under Mendes. I booked a double room for three nights.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Let me see... Yes, Ms. Mendes. I see you also requested a room with a view of the bay. I'm afraid those are all occupied tonight, but one will be free tomorrow. Would you like to move then?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: That's fine. Actually, could you also tell me what time breakfast is served? I have an early meeting.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Breakfast starts at six thirty in the restaurant on the second floor. And if you're in a hurry, we can prepare a takeaway box.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Perfect. I'll pick one up tomorrow at six forty-five.

transcript.speaker: Woman 1
transcript.text: OK, the last item is the venue for the product launch in May. Raj, did you hear back from the Lakeside Conference Center?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: I did. They're available on the date we want, but their main hall only holds about one hundred and fifty people.

transcript.speaker: Woman 2
transcript.text: That won't work. More than two hundred people have already signed up.

transcript.speaker: Woman 1
transcript.text: What about the Grandview Hotel? Didn't we use it for the sales conference last year?

transcript.speaker: Woman 2
transcript.text: We did, and the feedback was very positive. The only drawback is that it's a bit far from the train station.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: We could arrange a shuttle bus from the station. I'll call the hotel this afternoon to check availability.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Kelly, have you finished the quarterly sales figures? Mr. Tanaka wants them before the board meeting tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Almost. But the spreadsheet keeps freezing every time I try to add the data from the Asian branches.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That happened to me last month. It's because the file is too big. Try splitting it into two files, one for each region.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Good idea. But I've never done that before.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: I've got a few minutes now.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Oh, thanks! Let me save what I've done so far, then.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Hello, I'd like to book a table for this Friday evening for a group of twelve. It's for a colleague's farewell dinner.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: For twelve people, we'd recommend our private dining room. It comes with a set menu at forty-five dollars per person.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That sounds good. Would it be possible to bring our own cake? It's a surprise.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Of course. Just let our staff know when you arrive, and we'll keep it in the refrigerator until dessert.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Wonderful. Could you put the reservation under Lewis? We'll arrive around seven.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Done. I'll send a confirmation to your phone.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Hi, I'm in suite 410. The heating in our office hasn't been working since Monday, and it's getting really cold.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I'm sorry about that. Several offices on your floor have reported the same issue. The technician thinks a part in the boiler needs replacing.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Do you know how long that will take?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: The part has been ordered, but it won't arrive until Friday. In the meantime, we can lend you a couple of portable heaters.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That would help a lot. Could someone bring them up this morning?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I'll have our maintenance assistant deliver them within the hour.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Hi, I'm calling about an order I received yesterday. I ordered a black office chair, but the one that arrived is gray.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: I apologize for that, Ms. Becker. Could you give me your order number?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Sure, it's five, eight, two, seven, one.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Thank you. I see the mistake. The black model was out of stock, and our warehouse shipped the gray one without contacting you. We can send a black chair next week, and a courier will pick up the gray one at the same time.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Actually, the gray one matches my desk better than I expected. Is there any way I could just keep it?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Certainly. And for the inconvenience, I'll apply a fifteen percent discount to your next order.

transcript.speaker: Man 1
transcript.text: So, we've interviewed all four candidates for the data analyst position. What did you think?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I was really impressed by Ms. Okonkwo. Her experience with financial modeling is exactly what we need.

transcript.speaker: Man 2
transcript.text: I agree, but she said she can't start until September. We need someone by July at the latest.

transcript.speaker: Man 1
transcript.text: Well, the second candidate, Mr. Fischer, could start right away.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: True, but he's never worked with our software.

transcript.speaker: Man 2
transcript.text: That can be learned. Training only takes a couple of weeks.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Even so, why don't we ask HR whether we could bring in a contractor until September? That way we can still hire Ms. Okonkwo.

transcript.speaker: Man 1
transcript.text: I'll e-mail HR right after this.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Marcus, I just saw the agenda for next week's conference. Your presentation is scheduled for eight A.M. on Saturday.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Saturday? I was told it would be Friday afternoon. I've already booked my flight home for Friday night.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: The organizers must have changed it after adding a keynote speaker on Friday.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Well, I can't exactly miss my own presentation.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Why don't you call the airline? Some fares let you change the date for a small fee.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: I'll check my booking first. If that doesn't work, I'll ask the organizers whether someone could swap time slots with me.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Have you heard about the new bike-share program the city is launching next month?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Yes, there's going to be a station right outside our building. I'm thinking of signing up.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Me too. The bus has been so crowded lately, and a bike would get me here in fifteen minutes.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: And the company might even cover part of the membership. HR sent an e-mail about it this morning.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Really? I must have missed it. Do you know how to apply?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: You fill out a form on the intranet. The deadline is this Friday.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Lina, have you signed up for one of the customer service workshops yet? Everyone on the team has to attend at least one this month.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Not yet. I wanted to do the one on handling complaints, but I'm visiting clients all day Monday.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That's a shame. It's supposed to be the most useful. What about the e-mail session?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Hmm, on Wednesday morning I'm interviewing interns, and I'm off on Thursday. So the only one that works for me is on Tuesday.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That's a good one, too. Most of our calls are from customers asking about delivery dates.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Right. I'll register online right now.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Hi, I'm organizing a trade show booth for my company next month, and I need some printed materials.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Sure. What did you have in mind?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Originally I wanted brochures, but my budget is limited. I think I'll go with something cheaper that we can hand out to lots of people.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Then I'd recommend our flyers. You get a thousand of them, printed on high-quality paper.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That sounds perfect. How soon could they be ready?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: If you send us your design by tomorrow, we can have them done in three business days.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Our meeting with the client in Bristol starts at eleven thirty, and the trip takes about an hour.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Then we should take the nine forty. That gives us time to get from the station to their office.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Look at the board, though. That one's delayed by thirty minutes.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Hmm, that would be too tight. And anything later is out of the question.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Then let's take the earlier one. We can review the presentation on the train.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Good idea. I'll get us some coffee while you buy the tickets.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers mainly discussing?
questions.explanation: Toute la conversation porte sur le papier commandé qui n'est pas arrivé à cause d'un problème d'entrepôt.
questions.trap: « printer paper » évoque une imprimante, mais elle ne fonctionne pas mal ; les manuels de formation ne sont qu'un détail.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say will happen on Wednesday?
options: A supplier will visit the office.
questions.explanation: Elle dit : « We're printing the training manuals for the new hires on Wednesday ».
questions.trap: La commande arrivera jeudi, pas mercredi.

questions.prompt: What does the woman ask the man to do?
questions.explanation: Dernière réplique : « Just keep the receipt so accounting can reimburse you ».
questions.trap: L'homme a déjà appelé le fournisseur ; elle ne lui demande pas de recommencer.

questions.prompt: Where most likely are the speakers?
questions.explanation: « welcome to the Harbor View Hotel », réservation, chambre double : ils sont à la réception d'un hôtel.
questions.trap: Le petit-déjeuner est servi au restaurant de l'hôtel, mais la scène se passe à l'accueil.

questions.prompt: What problem does the man mention?
options: A room with a view is not available tonight.
The restaurant is closed for renovation.
The hotel is fully booked for three nights.
questions.explanation: « I'm afraid those are all occupied tonight, but one will be free tomorrow » : les chambres avec vue sont toutes prises ce soir.
questions.trap: L'hôtel n'est pas complet : seule la catégorie avec vue est indisponible ce soir.

questions.prompt: What will the woman probably pick up tomorrow morning?
questions.explanation: L'homme propose une boîte à emporter ; elle répond qu'elle en prendra une à 6 h 45.
questions.trap: Le changement de chambre aura lieu demain, mais la question porte sur ce qu'elle récupère le matin.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers discussing?
options: Choosing a location for an event
questions.explanation: « the venue for the product launch » : ils cherchent un lieu pour le lancement du produit.
questions.trap: La conférence commerciale de l'an dernier n'est évoquée que comme référence.

questions.prompt: Why is the Lakeside Conference Center unsuitable?
options: It is far from the station.
questions.explanation: La salle accueille environ 150 personnes alors que plus de 200 sont inscrites.
questions.trap: Le défaut « loin de la gare » concerne l'hôtel Grandview, pas Lakeside ; Lakeside est disponible à la date voulue.

questions.prompt: What will the man do this afternoon?
questions.explanation: « I'll call the hotel this afternoon to check availability. »
questions.trap: Il évoque une navette (« We could arrange a shuttle bus »), mais seulement comme possibilité.

questions.prompt: What problem does the woman mention?
questions.explanation: « the spreadsheet keeps freezing every time I try to add the data » : le tableur se bloque.
questions.trap: Les données asiatiques existent ; c'est leur ajout qui fait planter le fichier.

questions.prompt: What does the man suggest?
questions.explanation: « Try splitting it into two files, one for each region. » « splitting » est paraphrasé par « dividing ».
questions.trap: Repérer la paraphrase : le mot « split » n'apparaît pas dans l'option correcte.

questions.prompt: Why does the man say, “I've got a few minutes now”?
options: To explain that he must leave
To ask for the figures immediately
questions.explanation: Elle vient de dire qu'elle n'a jamais divisé un fichier ; il propose implicitement de lui montrer, et elle le remercie.
questions.trap: Interpréter littéralement « a few minutes » comme une contrainte de temps.

questions.prompt: Why is the man calling?
questions.explanation: « I'd like to book a table for this Friday evening » : il réserve une table.
questions.trap: Le gâteau est un détail ; il l'apportera lui-même.

questions.prompt: What is being celebrated?
questions.explanation: « a colleague's farewell dinner » : un dîner d'adieu, donc le départ d'un collègue.
questions.trap: Le gâteau surprise fait penser à un anniversaire.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say the staff will do?
questions.explanation: « we'll keep it in the refrigerator until dessert » : le personnel conservera le gâteau.
questions.trap: Le menu est fixe (« set menu ») ; il n'est pas préparé spécialement.

questions.prompt: Who most likely is the woman?
questions.explanation: Elle centralise les signalements des bureaux, commande la pièce et envoie un assistant de maintenance : elle gère l'immeuble.
questions.trap: Le technicien est mentionné, mais à la troisième personne (« The technician thinks… »).

questions.prompt: According to the woman, what will happen on Friday?
options: A new boiler will be installed.
questions.explanation: « The part has been ordered, but it won't arrive until Friday. »
questions.trap: On remplace une pièce de la chaudière, pas toute la chaudière.

questions.prompt: What does the woman offer to provide?
questions.explanation: « we can lend you a couple of portable heaters ».
questions.trap: Aucune compensation financière n'est proposée.

questions.prompt: Why is the woman calling?
questions.explanation: Elle a commandé une chaise noire et en a reçu une grise.
questions.trap: La commande est bien arrivée (hier) et la chaise n'est pas abîmée.

questions.prompt: What does the woman decide to do?
options: Return the chair for a refund
questions.explanation: « the gray one matches my desk better than I expected. Is there any way I could just keep it? »
questions.trap: La solution d'abord proposée (échange la semaine prochaine) n'est finalement pas retenue.

questions.prompt: What does the man offer?
options: A discount on a future purchase
questions.explanation: « I'll apply a fifteen percent discount to your next order ».
questions.trap: « next order » : la remise porte sur une prochaine commande, pas sur celle-ci.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers discussing?
questions.explanation: Ils comparent les candidats interviewés pour le poste d'analyste.
questions.trap: La formation au logiciel et le prestataire sont des éléments secondaires de la discussion.

questions.prompt: What concern is raised about Ms. Okonkwo?
questions.explanation: « she can't start until September. We need someone by July » : sa date de prise de poste pose problème.
questions.trap: C'est M. Fischer qui ne connaît pas le logiciel ; Mme Okonkwo, elle, a l'expérience recherchée.

questions.prompt: What does the woman suggest?
questions.explanation: « bring in a contractor until September » : faire appel à un prestataire temporaire.
questions.trap: « contractor » est paraphrasé par « temporary worker » ; la durée de formation est évoquée par l'autre homme.

questions.prompt: What did the woman just see?
questions.explanation: « I just saw the agenda for next week's conference ».
questions.trap: Le vol est évoqué par l'homme, pas vu par la femme.

questions.prompt: What does the man imply when he says, “I can't exactly miss my own presentation”?
options: He plans to skip the conference.
He wants a colleague to present instead.
He will have to change his travel plans.
He is unhappy with his presentation topic.
questions.explanation: Comme il ne peut pas manquer sa présentation du samedi, c'est son vol du vendredi soir qui doit changer.
questions.trap: Comprendre la phrase littéralement, comme une intention de ne pas venir.

questions.prompt: What will the man most likely do first?
questions.explanation: « I'll check my booking first. If that doesn't work, I'll ask the organizers… »
questions.trap: Demander aux organisateurs n'est que la solution de repli.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers mainly discussing?
questions.explanation: « the new bike-share program the city is launching » est le sujet de toute la conversation.
questions.trap: Le bus n'est cité que pour expliquer l'intérêt de l'homme.

questions.prompt: Why is the man interested in the program?
options: He recently moved closer to work.
questions.explanation: « The bus has been so crowded lately ».
questions.trap: L'exercice physique est une raison plausible, mais elle n'est jamais mentionnée.

questions.prompt: According to the woman, what must be done by Friday?
options: An information session must be attended.
questions.explanation: « You fill out a form on the intranet. The deadline is this Friday. »
questions.trap: L'entreprise pourrait payer une partie de l'abonnement ; aucun paiement n'est exigé vendredi.

questions.prompt: What must all team members do this month?
questions.explanation: « Everyone on the team has to attend at least one this month. »
questions.trap: Les visites de clients et les entretiens concernent seulement l'emploi du temps de la femme.

questions.prompt: Why can't the woman attend the session on Monday?
questions.explanation: « I'm visiting clients all day Monday. »
questions.trap: Les entretiens de stagiaires ont lieu mercredi, pas lundi.

questions.prompt: Look at the graphic. Which session will the woman most likely attend?
questions.explanation: Elle dit que seule la séance du mardi lui convient ; d'après le tableau, le mardi correspond à « Phone Etiquette ».
questions.trap: « Handling Complaints » est la séance qu'elle aurait voulu suivre, mais elle est le lundi.

questions.prompt: Where does the woman most likely work?
questions.explanation: Elle propose des produits imprimés, donne des délais d'impression et une liste de prix : elle travaille dans une imprimerie.
questions.trap: Le salon professionnel est l'événement du client, pas le lieu de travail de la femme.

questions.prompt: Look at the graphic. How much will the man most likely pay?
questions.explanation: Il renonce aux brochures et choisit les flyers recommandés ; le tableau indique 120 $ pour 1 000 flyers.
questions.trap: 210 $ correspond aux brochures qu'il voulait au départ.

questions.prompt: What does the woman ask the man to send?
questions.explanation: « If you send us your design by tomorrow… ».
questions.trap: Aucun acompte n'est mentionné.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the speakers' trip?
questions.explanation: « Our meeting with the client in Bristol starts at eleven thirty. »
questions.trap: La présentation qu'ils reverront dans le train est destinée au client, pas à une conférence.

questions.prompt: Look at the graphic. Which platform will the speakers go to?
questions.explanation: Le 9 h 40 est retardé et tout départ plus tardif est exclu : ils prennent le train précédent, celui de 9 h 15, qui part du quai 4.
questions.trap: Le quai 2 est celui du 9 h 40 qu'ils voulaient prendre au départ.

questions.prompt: What will the woman do next?
questions.explanation: « I'll get us some coffee while you buy the tickets. »
questions.trap: C'est l'homme qui achète les billets.
